about.title: Personal Injury Help in Malibu, California
about.longDescription: Malibu's roads carry a mix of daily commuters, tourists, and coastal traffic, and that mix shows up in the public collision numbers. In the most recent recorded year, Malibu saw 75 injury collisions and 115 people injured, with reports tending to cluster on Sunday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Corridors like Pacific Coast Highway (Rt 1) and Malibu Canyon Road account for a large share of these reported incidents, reflecting the volume of traffic that moves through this stretch of coastline every week. If you or someone you love has been hurt in a crash or another type of accident here, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and next steps can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. We handle personal injury claims in Malibu and throughout Los Angeles County. Our team can review the details of what happened and help you understand your options. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for you. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't commit you to anything.

items.title: You Have Limited Time
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months. Talking to us early helps make sure that window doesn't close on you.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Black and White
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible for the accident — your share of fault only reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate your claim.

items.title: No Cap on What You May Recover
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering, which can matter a great deal depending on how the injury has affected your life.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover compensation for you. There's no retainer and no bill just for having a conversation.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a claim after an accident in Malibu?
items.answer: In most personal injury cases in California, you have two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved — such as a city or county vehicle — that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Malibu?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reported crashes in Malibu are concentrated along corridors like Pacific Coast Highway (Rt 1) and Malibu Canyon Road, with a noticeable pattern of reports on Sunday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply public-record counts of where and when collisions have been reported, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery amount would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't bar you from making a claim entirely.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we recover money on your behalf. Reaching out to see what your options are doesn't cost anything upfront.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims in Malibu and across Los Angeles County. Our team can evaluate your situation and help you understand your options. We work on contingency and there's no fee unless we recover compensation for you.
